question: On 9 December 2025, the Commissioner for Health and Animal Welfare, Olivér Várhelyi, announced a 50 % increase in audits in non-EU countries and a 33 % increase in checks at border control posts. However, the Commission’s publicly available reports contain no consolidated overview of the actual number of checks carried out. 1.
What is the exact number of audits in non-EU countries and checks at border control posts carried out in 2025 on which the announced percentage increases are based?
When will the report under Article 114 of Regulation (EU) 2017/625 for the year 2023 and subsequent years be published, and why does the delay in reporting currently stand at almost two years?
How many additional auditors and inspectors are required to deliver the announced increase, and has the necessary budget already been approved?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (22.6.2026) In 2025, the Commission carried out 28 export-related onsite audits of third countries, and five onsite audits of Member States on official controls at border control posts. The Commission will publish in 2026 the report under Article 114 of Regulation (EU) 2017/6251 related to the years 2023 and 2024.

The timing is contingent on the availability of the annual reports to be submitted by the Member States and on the need to deliver on several competing priorities. The Commission will deliver on the announced increase by prioritising the control activities accordingly.

As detailed in the 2026 Health and Food Audits and Analysis work programme2, the Commission plans to perform 47 export-related onsite audits of third countries and seven onsite audits of Member States on official controls at border control posts.
1 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX:32017R0625. 2 Directorate-General for Health and Food Safety, Health and food audits and analysis programme – 2026,
